standards.name: Pathogen Transmission Ontology (TRANS)
standards.abstract: This resource models transmission methods of human disease pathogens — how a pathogen is transmitted from one host, reservoir, or source to another host. The subject matter covers both direct and indirect transmission routes and includes cases involving animate vectors or inanimate vehicles. The standard itself is an ontology (OWL/OBO) maintained as part of the Disease Ontology project and published under a CC0 license; it provides a hierarchical (DAG) representation of transmission process classes with persistent URIs, human-readable labels and curator-written definitions, synonyms, and status metadata.

classification.rationale: The source material is an ontology that organizes transmission processes hierarchically and uses explicit subclass (rdfs:subClassOf) relationships between terms. The document describes the data as a directed acyclic graph and declares classes and SubClassOf statements (i.e., nodes and edges), so the native structure is a DAG rather than a flat field table or a prose checklist.

TRANS_0000000.name: transmission process
TRANS_0000000.description: A process that is the means during which the pathogen is transmitted directly or indirectly from its natural reservoir, a susceptible host or source to a new host.
TRANS_0000000.evidence: A process that is the means during which the pathogen is transmitted directly or indirectly from its natural reservoir, a susceptible host or source to a new host.

TRANS_0000001.name: direct transmission
TRANS_0000001.description: Direct transmission is a transmission process that is the means during which the pathogen is transmitted immediately from a reservoir, source or host to another host.
TRANS_0000001.evidence: Direct transmission is a transmission process that is the means during which the pathogen is transmitted immediately from a reservoir, source or host to another host.

TRANS_0000002.name: indirect transmission
TRANS_0000002.description: Indirect transmission is a transmission process during which the pathogen is indirectly transferred from a reservoir, source or host to another host by intermediary vehicles, vectors or as airborne dust particles.
TRANS_0000002.evidence: Indirect transmission is a transmission process during which the pathogen is indirectly transferred from a reservoir, source or host to another host by intermediary vehicles, vectors or as airborne dust particles.

TRANS_0000003.name: mechanical transmission
TRANS_0000003.description: Mechanical transmission is an indirect vector-borne transmission process during which the pathogen is indirectly transferred from a reservoir, source or host to another host by being transported on the external surface of the vector.
TRANS_0000003.evidence: Mechanical transmission is an indirect vector-borne transmission process during which the pathogen is indirectly transferred from a reservoir, source or host to another host by being transported on the external surface of the vector.

errors.detail: Graph is not fully connected; unreachable node(s) from an arbitrary start

standards.notes: Primary source quotes and ontology content were taken from the Disease Ontology Pathogen Transmission Ontology web pages and the included trans.owl / trans-edit.owl files (DC description and IAO_0000115 annotations). The ontology is released under CC0 and is part of the Disease Ontology project.
